latest_release.name: v2.1.0
latest_release.body:
The first feature release after v2.0.0, with the security fixes of Node v24.22.3.

It is a release full of fixes and new features made by the wonderful Freelens community, and special thanks go to everyone who contributed to it.

## What's new:

v2.1.0 brings themes as files with eight built-in themes, a choice of accent color and zoom level, overviews as cards, combined logs for the pods of a workload, debugging a pod in an ephemeral container, copying the values of the details in one click, the certificate details of secrets, the mutating admission policies, metrics for GKE clusters from Google Managed Prometheus, and Helm releases read straight from the Kubernetes API. The extension API gains a credential store encrypted with the secret store of the system, the certificate view of secrets, the overview cards, the copy controls and the generic components the views of Freelens are built from. It also fixes the connection to clusters whose kubeconfig has a colon in its file name or is written in UTF-16, Windows shells given by name, custom extension registries served under a path, the metrics of several setups, and several issues of the logs, the sidebar and the details.

### New Features

* Themes are YAML files with a dark and a light variant, chosen in Preferences → Personalization. Eight are built in: Freelens, Ayu, Ayu Mirage, Dracula, Graphite, Catppuccin, Solarized and High Contrast, whose text reaches a contrast of 7:1. A theme can be exported, and imported from a file or a URL. See [the theme format](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/blob/main/docs/themes.md). See #3029, #3035, #3036, #3037, #3038, #3040, #3041, #3043, #3045, #3049, #3046, #3052, #3047, #3054, #3053, #3055
* The accent color can be chosen for the dark and the light variant, from named swatches or as any color, with a palette and a field for its hex code. See #1280, #1431, #3032, #3033, #3034
* Preferences → Personalization sets the zoom level, from 67% to 200%, and keeps it across restarts. See #3044, #3050
* The cluster overview and the workloads overview can show cards that state the numbers, with line charts for the cluster metrics, instead of the ring and pie charts. Overview style in Preferences → Personalization chooses them. See #3042, #3051
* Combined logs for a workload: the Logs item of a Deployment, DaemonSet, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet or Job opens one tab with the logs of all its pods, interleaved by time, each pod in a colour of its own. A new preference under Kubernetes sets how many pods such a tab reads. See #687, #2418, #3004, #3006
* The details of a secret show the certificates it holds in PEM: subject, issuer, DNS names and IP addresses, serial number, validity, and the expiry, marked when it is near or past. The certificates are parsed in the main process. See #3002, #3003, #3008, #3010
* MutatingAdmissionPolicies and MutatingAdmissionPolicyBindings under Config, next to the validating ones, on clusters that serve them as v1, v1beta1 or v1alpha1. The details of the validating and mutating policies and bindings show their namespace and object selectors. See #2434, #2511
* The Google Managed Prometheus provider reads the GKE system metrics, which GKE collects for every cluster at no extra charge, through the query frontend of Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus. The cluster, nodes, pods, workloads and PVCs get their charts without node-exporter or kube-state-metrics. Auto Detect finds the frontend, and the Metrics settings of the cluster link to Google's instructions for deploying it. See #3097, #3099, #3107
* The ingresses list has a Class column, and the details of an ingress show its IngressClass, with a link when it comes from `spec.ingressClassName`. See #2936, #2945
* The General settings of a cluster set an Icon Label of up to four characters and an Icon Color, so that the clusters of one environment look alike in every region. See #1908, #2994
* The pods list and the pods of a workload have a Ports column, search

[Freelens](https://freelens.app) is a free and open-source user interface designed for managing Kubernetes clusters. It provides a standalone application compatible with macOS, Windows, and Linux operating systems, making it accessible to a wide range of users. The application aims to simplify the complexities of Kubernetes management by offering an intuitive and user-friendly interface.
## Requirements Kubernetes 1.22 or later. Older clusters fall back to the bundled `kubectl`, which may not work correctly; a different one can be set in Preferences. ## Downloads See the [releases](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/releases) page and download the right package for your system. ### macOS macOS 13 or later is required. Download either the PKG (installer) or DMG (image) package from the [releases](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/releases) page. Both arm64 (M1 chip or newer) and amd64 (Intel) variants are available. All binary packages are built on macOS 15 and should be compatible with newer systems. #### Homebrew Run the following command: ```sh brew install --cask freelens ``` ### Linux Linux with GNU C Library 2.34 or later is required. It is provided ie. by Debian 12, Fedora 35, Mint 21, openSUSE Leap 15.4, Ubuntu 22.04 and by rolling release distributions like Arch, Manjaro or Tumbleweed. Download DEB or RPM (package) or AppImage (executable) from the [releases](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/releases) page. Both arm64 (aarch64) and amd64 (x86_64) variants are available. All binary packages are built on Ubuntu 22.04 and should be compatible with new systems. #### AppImage The Linux AppImage file requires libz.so and libfuse.so.2. You can add them by running: ```sh sudo apt install libfuse2 zlib1g-dev ``` Run the application with additional arguments: ```sh ./Freelens*.AppImage --no-sandbox --ozone-platform-hint=auto --enable-features=WebRTCPipeWireCapturer --enable-features=WaylandWindowDecorations --disable-gpu-compositing ``` #### Flatpak The package is available on the [Flathub](https://flathub.org/apps/app.freelens.Freelens) App Store for Linux. Use GNOME Software application or run the following commands: ```sh flatpak install flathub app.freelens.Freelens flatpak run app.freelens.Freelens ``` The application is sandboxed. It includes bundled `kubectl` and `helm` commands and uses the `~/.kube/config` file by default. Flatpak adds wrappers for the `aws`, `doctl`, `gke-gcloud-auth-plugin`, and `kubelogin` tools, running them as commands from the host system. The terminal uses `/bin/sh` by default, but it can be switched to, for example, `/bin/bash` for a sandboxed environment or `/app/bin/host-spawn` for a host environment. #### Snap The package is available on the [Snap](https://snapcraft.io/freelens) Store for Linux. Use App Center application or run the following command: ```sh snap install freelens --classic ``` #### APT repository Run the following commands: ```sh curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/freelensapp/freelens/refs/heads/main/freelens/build/apt/freelens.asc | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/freelens.asc curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/freelensapp/freelens/refs/heads/main/freelens/build/apt/freelens.sources | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/freelens.sources sudo apt update sudo apt install freelens ``` #### Arch User Repository The package is available on the [Arch User Repository (AUR)](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Arch_User_Repository). Check the [freelens-bin](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/freelens-bin) package page. #### Secret store Extensions keep tokens and passwords encrypted with the desktop's secret store: GNOME Keyring or another Secret Service provider through libsecret, or KWallet. The application finds it on its own on GNOME, KDE, Cinnamon, XFCE and other common desktops. On a desktop it does not recognise, such as sway, Hyprland or i3, the extensions cannot keep such values, so name the secret store when you start the application: ```sh freelens --password-store=gnome-libsecret ``` Use `gnome-libsecret` for any Secret Service provider, such as GNOME Keyring or KeePassXC, and `kwallet5` or `kwallet6` for KWallet. The provider must be running in the session. The AppImage and `flatpak run app.freelens.Freelens` take the same argument. ### Windows Windows 10 or later is required. Download the EXE (NSIS) or MSI installers from the [releases](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/releases) page. Both the x64 (amd64) and arm64 versions of the Windows binaries are provided. However, an EXE installer (NSIS) itself is x86 binary only even if it installs arm64 application and then installs to `C:\Program Files (x86)\Freelens` path by default. The version of the MSI package has the last 4th digit always `0` and this is a limitation of this package format. #### Portable Download the Portable EXE from the [releases](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/releases) page. It is a self-contained executable that can be run without installation. #### WinGet The package is available in [WinGet](https://winstall.app/apps/Freelensapp.Freelens) Community [repository](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs). Run the following command: ```powershell winget install Freelensapp.Freelens ``` The `--silent` option is supported to suppress all UI. The `--scope user` or `--scope machine` option can be used to install it either to local user directory or to `C:\Program Files`. WinGet installs the application from EXE installer (NSIS). #### Scoop The package is available in the [Scoop](https://scoop.sh/#/apps?q=freelens&s=1&d=0) command-line installer for Windows. Run the following command: ```powershell scoop bucket add extras scoop install freelens ``` Scoop uses MSI package to install the application. #### WSL The terminal can run a WSL shell: set the shell to `wsl.exe` in the terminal preferences. The `kubectl` and `helm` commands of the WSL distribution then use the cluster opened in Freelens. WSL 2 requires the mirrored networking mode. Add it to the `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` file: ```ini [wsl2] networkingMode=mirrored ``` Then restart WSL with `wsl --shutdown`. ## Development Visit the [Development](DEVELOPMENT.md) document to see how to build the application from source. Check out the [Freelens Docs](https://freelensapp.github.io/docs/) to contribute to development or create your own extension. ## Extensions Anyone can develop extensions for Freelens and many extensions previously used with Open Lens have already been converted. Visit the [Extensions](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/discussions/2291) discussion to see them and write in the [appropriate discussion](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/discussions/117) if you also want to propose yours. The skills for coding agents that create Freelens extensions and port v1 extensions to the v2 extension API are the `freelens` plugin of [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins), whose `SKILL.md` files in [`plugins/freelens/skills`](plugins/freelens/skills) other agents read too. Add the marketplace with `--sparse`, which checks out only the plugin instead of the whole Freelens repository, then install the plugin from it: ```sh claude plugin marketplace add freelensapp/freelens --sparse .claude-plugin plugins claude plugin install freelens@freelens ``` `/freelens:create-extension` starts a new extension from a copy of [freelens-example-extension](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens-example-extension), and `/freelens:port-extension-to-v2` ports an extension written for the v1 extension API. ## Community Get updates about Freelens & keep in touch with our community - Follow us on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/freelensapp/) - Follow us on [Bluesky](https://bsky.app/profile/freelensapp.bsky.social) - Follow us on [X](https://x.com/freelensapp) - Join our [Discussions](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/discussions) - Chat on [Discord](https://discord.gg/NjKZERK95Y) - Discuss on [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/freelens/) - Watch us on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@Freelensapp) - Open an [Issue](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/issues) ## Adopters Freelens is used by many individuals, companies, and organizations. We have created the [adopters](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/blob/main/ADOPTERS.md) file for anyone who would like to be part of the official list. Anyone is welcome to request to be added to the official list by opening a dedicated Pull Request. ## Contributing Anyone is welcome to collaborate to advance the Freelens project. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) to see how you can help. ## Expenses and Donations Anyone can support the Freelens project by making donations to cover maintenance costs and invest in its development. For more information, see our dedicated discussion: [Expenses and Donations](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/discussions/2292) ## Fund an issue or earn money by developing Anyone who wishes can also make targeted donations, funding their preferred issues alone or with others via [BountyHub](https://www.bountyhub.dev/en/bounties?repo=freelens). At the same time, anyone who wishes can apply by doing PR to earn the bounty. Features are, in any case, decided democratically according to the community's wishes and overseen by the Freelens core team. For more information, see our dedicated discussion: [Fund an issue or earn money by developing](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/discussions/2293) ## The Freelens Teams ### Core Team Each member of the core team is focused on specific roles. You can contact us at any time according to them. - [Roberto Bandini](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bandiniroberto/) - [@robertobandini](https://github.com/robertobandini) - Founder
General organization management, relationships, product management, community, marketing, extensions ecosystem (review, catalog, strategy and development) - [Piotr Roszatycki](https://www.linkedin.com/in/piotr.roszatycki) - [@dex4er](https://github.com/dex4er) - Maintainer
Development direction, architecture and release management, extensions development - [Mario Offertucci](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mario-offertucci-703113b6/) - [@mariomamo](https://github.com/mariomamo) - Maintainer
UI, docs, extensions development - [Leopoldo Capuano](https://www.linkedin.com/in/leo-capuano/) - [@leo-capvano](https://github.com/leo-capvano) - Maintainer
GenAI solutions, extensions development ### Release Engineering Team This team is responsible for driving Freelens releases forward, reviewing PRs, and making decisions about the architecture and technical roadmap under the supervision of the core team. - [Piotr Roszatycki](https://www.linkedin.com/in/piotr.roszatycki) - [@dex4er](https://github.com/dex4er) - Maintainer
Release Engineering Team Lead - [Omar Alani](https://www.linkedin.com/in/omarluq/) - [@omarluq](https://github.com/omarluq) - Maintainer
Release Engineering Team Member - [Matías Roje](https://www.linkedin.com/in/matias-roje-carrasco/) - [@MatiasRoje](https://github.com/MatiasRoje) - Maintainer
Release Engineering Team Member The project is growing very quickly and everyone is welcome! If you also want to be part of it, visit the [We want you!](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/discussions/2297) discussion. Or contact us at for any questions or suggestions! ## License This repository is a fork of [Open Lens](https://github.com/lensapp/lens/tree/master), the core of [Lens Desktop](https://k8slens.dev), with the aim of carrying forward its open-source version.
